seed_ledger.name: VoltaGrid SAT-2 Power Plant (gas supply)
seed_ledger.reason: NOT_FOUND: one of two off-grid Vantage data center campuses on the west side of San Antonio, with about 423 MW of gas generation behind the meter. The Environmental Integrity Project release, the Texas Public Radio and San Antonio Current lawsuit stories, Data Center Dynamics, Baxtel, Microgrid Knowledge and the law firm summary of the notice of intent describe the plants as gas-fired and behind the meter but name no pipeline, tap, lateral or gas supplier. Energy Transfer is named only for VoltaGrid's separate Oracle sites. FERC, Railroad Commission and TCEQ permit files could not be read through search; no result pointed to them. Searches run: 9. Sources checked: EIP release (no gas supply), TPR (no pipeline), SA Current (no pipeline), Microgrid Knowledge (generic), Deceleration (nothing on gas), Cleanview (Energy Transfer for Oracle sites only).

evidence.note: gas-fired behind-the-meter plants for San Antonio data centers; no gas supply named

seed_ledger.name: Waha to Mexico (Wahalajara System Expansion)
seed_ledger.reason: Length unknown, no new US pipe and no US data center tie. The expansion adds two turbo-compression units at San Juan in Chihuahua and at Aguascalientes in Mexico, raising capacity from about 1.3 to about 2 Bcf/d, in service 2027. Siemens Energy lists data centers only as a Mexican demand sector. Trade press (Pipeline and Gas Journal, Turbomachinery, Enerdata) and a FERC-focused search showed no US filing or US facility. Searches run: 4. Sources checked: Siemens Energy release (Mexican compression, data centers named generically), P&GJ March 2026 (route from Waha, no US scope), EIA row (power and industrial demand in Mexico), FERC search (nothing on this project).

evidence.note: compression units in Mexico; data centers named only as Mexican demand sector

seed_ledger.name: Data City Energy Center (gas supply)
seed_ledger.reason: NOT_FOUND: Energy Abundance Development Corp plans a behind-the-meter campus near Laredo, 300 MW first phase on Texas-produced gas, later hydrogen, up to 5 GW. The data center tie is real but the site is not definitively located and no pipeline, supplier, tap, air permit or filing was found. Nearest GGIT line is Tejas (P0258) at 6 km, unsourced. Searches run: 5. Sources checked: Connect CRE (plan, no pipeline), Baxtel and DC Byte listings (gas then hydrogen, no supplier), Webb County well records (unrelated), Laredo news and commissioner search (nothing on the project).

evidence.note: behind-the-meter Data City plan near Laredo; no gas supply named
